/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
## Summary

Port the Hysteria v2.14.0 UDP forwarding optimization
(HyNetworks/hysteria@c2b181e) to `proxy/hysteria`. The wire format is
unchanged; this only removes per-packet allocations.

Refs: https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/issues/7484

## Changes

- Parse UDP messages in place with `quicvarint.Parse`; add
  `ParseUDPMessageReuseAddr` and keep `ParseUDPMessage` as a wrapper.
- Reuse the packet buffer, `UDPMessage`, and `*net.Destination` in
  `UDPReader`; clone fragment data because `Defragger` retains it.
- Stack-allocate `UDPMessage` in `UDPWriter`, cache the last `b.UDP`
  and its string form, and use `errors.AsType` for
  `*quic.DatagramTooLargeError`.
- Update `apernet/quic-go` to v0.65.1 and adapt the MASQUE CONNECT-IP
  code to the new `HTTPStream() (*http3.Stream, error)` signature.

## Benchmarks

1200 B datagram, linux/amd64, 8 vCPU, medians:

| Path | Allocs/op | Time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `ParseUDPMessage` | 7 → 2 | ~277 → ~91 ns |
| `UDPWriter.WriteMultiBuffer` | 4 → 0 | ~235 → ~125 ns |
| `UDPReader.ReadFrom` | 12 → 0 | ~1395 → ~57 ns |
| `UDPReader.ReadMultiBuffer` | 15 → 3 | ~1763 → ~423 ns |

Writer numbers are for the writer itself; the benchmark's own
destination allocation is excluded. The remaining `ReadMultiBuffer`
allocations come from `common/buf`. The full harness and the
implementation transcript are in #7484.

## Compatibility

The Hysteria wire format does not change. Old and new Xray builds and
official Hysteria v2.14.0 peers remain interoperable. No config or API
changes.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`
- `go test -run '^$' ./...`
- `go test ./proxy/hysteria/... ./transport/internet/masque/...`
- `go test -race ./proxy/hysteria`
- `go run ./infra/vformat`

/issues?state=open&per_page=8.title: SS2022 (AES) UDP inbound: a UDP session is created before the packet is authenticated, so any junk datagram costs ~1.5 KB of memory until the next cleanup
/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
### Integrity requirements - [x] I have read all the comments in the issue template and ensured that this issue meet the requirements. - [x] I confirm that I have read the documentation, understand the meaning of all the configuration items I wrote, and did not pile up seemingly useful options or default values. - [x] I provided the complete config and logs, rather than just providing the truncated parts based on my own judgment. - [x] I searched issues and did not find any similar issues. - [x] The problem can be successfully reproduced in the latest Release ### Description On a Shadowsocks 2022 inbound with an AES method (`2022-blake3-aes-128-gcm` / `2022-blake3-aes-256-gcm`), single-user and multi-user, every UDP datagram of at least 43 bytes (multi-user) or 30 bytes (single-user) creates a `ServerUDPSession` before anything about the packet has been authenticated. The datagram does not have to come from a client or carry a valid key: random bytes are enough. `MultiUserInbound.processUDP` (`proxy/shadowsocks_2022/inbound_multi.go`) and `UDPCodec.DecodePacket` (`proxy/shadowsocks_2022/packet.go`, used by the single-user inbound) decrypt the 16-byte header with the block cipher, which always succeeds, take the session ID from it and call `udpSessions.GetOrCreate(sessionID)`, then `CheckPacketID`, which allocates the 1 KiB replay window. Only after that is the EIH looked up (multi-user) and the AEAD body opened. When the packet turns out to be junk, it is dropped, but the session stays in the map. Such a session never gets a link, so its inactivity timer never runs. It is removed only by `UDPSessionManager.cleanup`, which runs only when `GetOrCreate` creates a new session at least 30 seconds after the previous cleanup, and only for sessions idle for more than the timeout (500 s on both inbounds). On a server that receives nothing more after the junk, the memory is not released at all. Measured with the official `ghcr.io/xtls/xray-core:26.11.9` image (`Xray 26.11.9 Custom (go1.27.4 linux/arm64)`), the server config below, 100,000 random 48-byte datagrams from one source at 4,000/s over loopback, heap read from the `metrics` pprof endpoint with `?gc=1`: | inbound | HeapAlloc before | after 100k datagrams | 60 s later, no traffic | |---|---|---|---| | multi-user (AES-256) | 1.6 MB | 148.3 MB | 147.9 MB | | single-user (AES-256) | 1.5 MB | 149.1 MB | 148.6 MB | That is about 1.47 KB per datagram. A heap profile on `main` (b56ffef) attributes ~75 % to `(*ServerUDPSession).CheckPacketID` (the replay window) and the rest to `(*UDPSessionManager).GetOrCreate` and the sync.Map. On `main` I also left the server idle for 560 s after 50,000 junk datagrams: the 74 MB were still allocated, and they were freed when the next datagram arrived and triggered cleanup. Nothing is logged at any log level. Not affected: `2022-blake3-chacha20-poly1305` (the whole packet is opened before `GetOrCreate`), and the relay inbound (random data does not match a destination EIH). The cost is memory, not a crash or an authentication bypass: the junk is never dispatched. But the rate needed is low (a few thousand small datagrams per second fill hundreds of MB within the 500 s window), it needs no knowledge of the server, and on a small VPS it ends in an OOM kill of the whole process. I have a fix with a regression test, if the approach is acceptable I can open a PR: look the session up without creating it, open the AEAD body first (with the stored cipher of an existing session, or a new one derived from the PSK), and only then `GetOrCreate` the session and record the packet ID; the ChaCha path in `DecodePacket` likewise only checks the window of an existing session and creates it after the packet is validated. With it, the same 100,000 datagrams leave HeapAlloc at 1.6–1.7 MB; `go test -race ./proxy/shadowsocks_2022/` and the `TestShadowsocks2022*` tests in `testing/scenarios` pass, old and new builds interoperate in both directions (2000/2000 UDP echoes through a multi-user inbound; also 2000/2000 with a patched server while junk is being sent), and a decode benchmark shows no difference (~400 ns per 1200-byte packet). The new test sends a forged packet (a valid packet with the last byte flipped) and checks that no session was created; it fails on `main`. ### Reproduction Method 1. Start the server config below (any AES 2022 method; single-user behaves the same without `clients`). 2. Read the heap: `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:11111/debug/pprof/heap?gc=1&debug=1" | grep -E "^# Heap(Alloc|Objects) "` 3. Send random datagrams to the inbound with the program below: `go run . 127.0.0.1:8388 100000 4000 48` (any tool that sends random UDP works). 4. Read the heap again, right away and after a minute without traffic.
junk sender (Go)

/issues?state=open&per_page=8.title: Hysteria: reduce per-packet allocations in UDP forwarding
transport/internet: non-force DNS empty response is logged at error level without the domain
/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
### What version of Xray did you use?
26.11.9 (676eaf6). For comparison: 26.3.27 (d2758a0).

### Which operating system and architecture?
Linux amd64, official `Xray-linux-64.zip` builds.

### Minimal config
```json
{
  "log": {"loglevel": "debug", "access": "none"},
  "dns": {"queryStrategy": "UseIPv4", "servers": ["https://1.1.1.1/dns-query", "localhost"]},
  "inbounds": [{"listen":"127.0.0.1","port":19090,"protocol":"socks","settings":{"auth":"no","udp":false}}],
  "outbounds": [{"protocol":"freedom","settings":{"domainStrategy":"UseIP"}}]
}
```

### Steps to reproduce
```bash
curl -fsSL -o x.zip https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/releases/download/v26.11.9/Xray-linux-64.zip
unzip -q x.zip
./xray run -c cfg.json &
curl -sS --max-time 8 --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:19090 http://ipv6.google.com/
```
`ipv6.google.com` is AAAA-only; an A query returns CNAME + NOERROR/NODATA. Repeat with the 26.3.27 binary.

### What did you expect?
The A query returns NOERROR/NODATA. Because `UseIP` is a non-force strategy, `DialSystem` continues dialing with the domain and the system resolver may even connect on an IPv6-capable host. The expected behavior is an informational log line (as in 26.3.27), not an error per retry:
```
[Info] proxy/freedom: failed to get IP address for domain ipv6.google.com > features/dns: empty response
```

### What actually happened?
26.11.9 logs the failure at error level on every retry, and the domain is missing:
```
2026/11/25 03:02:37.280261 [Error] [840701999] transport/internet: failed to resolve ip > features/dns: empty response
2026/11/25 03:02:37.658563 [Error] [840701999] transport/internet: failed to resolve ip > features/dns: empty response
```
26.3.27, same config:
```
2026/11/25 03:02:41.314476 [Info] [3525449037] proxy/freedom: failed to get IP address for domain ipv6.google.com > features/dns: empty response
2026/11/25 03:02:41.723299 [Info] [3525449037] proxy/freedom: failed to get IP address for domain ipv6.google.com > features/dns: empty response
```

Real-world case: Facebook netseer measurement names like `<uuid>-netseer-ipaddr-assoc.xy.fbcdn.net` are AAAA-only by design. Each app session produces up to 5 error lines per connection (freedom retries); with `loglevel: error` this is the only visible output, and journal-based monitoring alerts on it.

### Suggested fix
1. Log at info/debug when `sockopt.DomainStrategy.ForceIP()` is false; keep error for force strategies.
2. Include the domain in the message, e.g. `failed to resolve ip for <domain>`, so operators can filter or route it.
3. Or do not log `ErrEmptyResponse` at error level for non-force strategies at all; return the error to the caller and let it decide.

### Notes
- 26.3.27 resolved the name inside `proxy/freedom` and logged at Info with the domain; 26.11.9 moved the lookup into `transport/internet.DialSystem`, so the domain is lost.
- Because the strategy is non-force, the dial continues after the log, so on an IPv6-capable host the connection may succeed. This is log noise, not necessarily a failed connection.
- Reproduced with both official binaries on the same config; 1.1.1.1 returns NOERROR/NODATA for the test name.

/issues?state=open&per_page=8.title: Hysteria, MASQUE, XDRIVE & XHTTP/3 clients: Close the packet conn before the QUIC transport
/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
When a client dials through `sockopt.dialerProxy`, its packet conn is a `FakePacketConn` over `cnc.Connection`, and `SetReadDeadline` on it does nothing. `quic.Transport.Close()` stops its read loop only through that deadline and then waits for the loop to return, so closing the transport before the packet conn blocks until the tunnel under it closes by itself.

In the Hysteria client this happens in `client.close()` with the client lock held, so every new dial on that outbound waits. I hit it with a Hysteria outbound behind another Hysteria outbound and an apernet Hysteria 2.14.0 server at the end (default `maxIdleTimeout` of 30s). After 35 seconds of idle the next request timed out, and the outbound stayed dead for about two minutes. With a request every 60 seconds it never recovered.

Fix: close the packet conn first, then the transport, as #7413 did for one XHTTP/3 path. This covers the Hysteria client and the same calls in MASQUE, XDRIVE and the XHTTP/3 `context.AfterFunc`. With the fix, the Hysteria setup above reconnects on the first request after idle: 0 failures in 36 requests, against two-minute stalls before.

/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
### Operating system

Linux

### System version

OpenWrt 25.12 (kernel 6.12, aarch64 Cortex-A76) for the field measurements; macOS 26 arm64 for the loopback reproduction

### Installation type

Original sing-box Command Line

### If you are using a graphical client, please provide the version of the client.

_No response_

### Version

```shell
sing-box version 1.14.5-0.20261124145405-6c65b2e63327 (testing)
Environment: go1.26.11
Tags: with_quic,with_gvisor,with_utls,with_clash_api
CGO: disabled
dependencies: sing-quic v0.7.2-0.20261124143824-14ca3448d44b, quic-go v0.61.0-sing-box-mod.15

compared with v1.14.4 (sing-quic 7e0a5869a5f4) built with the same toolchain and tags.
```

### Description

**1. Upload regression on `testing` (sing-quic fad401c979 "hysteria2: Fix salamander writes").**

v1.14.4 wrote obfuscated client packets through `VectorisedSalamanderConn.Write` (in-place XOR + writev). After fad401c979 the client goes through `SalamanderConn.Write`, which builds every datagram one byte at a time:

```go
for index, c := range p {
    common.Must(buffer.WriteByte(c ^ key[index%blake2b.Size256]))
}
```

A CPU profile of the hysteria2 client under bidirectional load shows `SalamanderConn.Write` at 37.7% of process CPU; `common.Must`, `Buffer.IsFull` and `Buffer.WriteByte` alone are about 3.5 s of a 16.1 s sample, while AES-GCM is under 5%.

Loopback, same machine, Salamander obfs, upload through the client, 3 interleaved runs of 15 s each (steps below):

| client and server build | upload Mbps | median |
|---|---|---:|
| v1.14.4 | 1474, 1490, 1509 | 1490 |
| testing 6c65b2e6 | 1324, 1339, 1355 | 1339 |
| testing 6c65b2e6 + patch below | 1804, 1885, 1893 | 1885 |

On a Linux ARM64 router (one hysteria2 connection, Gecko obfs, bidirectional load of 850 Mbps offered each way, `up_mbps`/`down_mbps` 930, interleaved runs) the same three builds gave 531–623, 469–536 and 603–614 Mbps upload, and the patched build used about 15% less CPU than v1.14.4.

The patch keeps the copy, so the caller's buffer is not mutated (which I assume is what fad401c979 fixed), and XORs in 32-byte strides with `crypto/subtle`. Its output is byte-identical to the original loop for every length from 0 to 2100 and round-trips through `SalamanderCodec`. It replaces the loops in `SalamanderConn.Read/Write`, `SalamanderPacketConn.ReadFrom/WriteTo` and `SalamanderCodec.Encode/Decode`:

```go
func salamanderXOR(dst, src []byte, key *[blake2b.Size256]byte) {
	for offset := 0; offset < len(src); offset += blake2b.Size256 {
		subtle.XORBytes(dst[offset:], src[offset:], key[:])
	}
}
```

for example in `SalamanderConn.Write`:

```go
-	for index, c := range p {
-		common.Must(buffer.WriteByte(c ^ key[index%blake2b.Size256]))
-	}
+	salamanderXOR(buffer.Extend(len(p)), p, &key)
```

**2. Obfuscated clients still cannot use GSO (feature request).**

14ca3448 hands raw sockets to quic-go on obfuscated servers through `PacketCodec`, but the client still wraps a connected `net.Conn` in `GeckoConn`/`SalamanderConn`, so quic-go runs `sendPacketsWithoutGSO`: one XOR and one `sendto` per datagram. On one connection under bidirectional load this is the main upload limit, because the run loop yields to received packets after every sent packet ("Prioritize receiving of packets over sending out more packets") and the send queue holds 8 packets.

On the router above, one connection with stock v1.14.4 reached 914 Mbps download-only and 725 Mbps upload-only, but about 850 down / 600 up at the same time. An experimental client build that applies Salamander per GSO segment and sends with `UDP_SEGMENT` (v1.14.4 otherwise) reached about 855 down / 815 up at the same time and 829 Mbps upload-only, with short-request latency unchanged at a 140 ms RTT.

Could the client use the same `PacketCodec` path as the server, so quic-go keeps GSO/GRO with obfuscation enabled?

+package hysteria2
+
+import (
+	"crypto/subtle"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/blake2b"
+)
+
+// salamanderXOR writes src XOR the repeating 32-byte Salamander key into dst.
+//
+// Contract used by every call site in salamander.go:
+//   - len(dst) >= len(src)
+//   - dst and src are either the same slice (in-place decode) or do not overlap
+//   - byte i of the output is src[i] ^ key[i%32], exactly like the original loop,
+//     so packets stay byte-for-byte compatible with stock Hysteria 2 peers.
+//
+// This runs once per UDP datagram on both send and receive, about 85k times per
+// second per direction at gigabit rates on the R6S, so it sits on the hot path.
+func salamanderXOR(dst, src []byte, key *[blake2b.Size256]byte) {
+	// Each 32-byte stride starts at key offset 0, matching key[i%32]; XORBytes stops at the
+	// shorter input, so the final partial stride needs no special case.
+	for offset := 0; offset < len(src); offset += blake2b.Size256 {
+		subtle.XORBytes(dst[offset:], src[offset:], key[:])
+	}
+}

+package hysteria2
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"crypto/rand"
+	"testing"
+

+)
+
+// reference is the original per-byte loop; the wire format must not change.
+func reference(src []byte, key *[blake2b.Size256]byte) []byte {
+	out := make([]byte, len(src))
+	for i := range src {
+		out[i] = src[i] ^ key[i%blake2b.Size256]
+	}
+	return out

### Reproduction

Local loopback only. Server (`server.json`):

```json
{"log":{"level":"error"},
 "inbounds":[{"type":"hysteria2","listen":"127.0.0.1","listen_port":34443,
   "obfs":{"type":"salamander","password":"loopback-obfs"},
   "users":[{"password":"loopback"}],
   "tls":{"enabled":true,"certificate_path":"cert.pem","key_path":"key.pem"}}]}
```

Client (`client.json`):

```json
{"log":{"level":"error"},
 "inbounds":[{"type":"mixed","listen":"127.0.0.1","listen_port":34080}],
 "outbounds":[{"type":"hysteria2","tag":"hy2","server":"127.0.0.1","server_port":34443,
   "password":"loopback","obfs":{"type":"salamander","password":"loopback-obfs"},
   "tls":{"enabled":true,"server_name":"loop.test","certificate_path":"cert.pem"}}],
 "route":{"final":"hy2"}}
```

1. `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 1 -subj /CN=loop.test -addext subjectAltName=DNS:loop.test`
2. `sing-box run -c server.json` and `sing-box run -c client.json`
3. Run a TCP sink on 127.0.0.1:34500 and push 4 TCP streams through `HTTP CONNECT 127.0.0.1:34500` on 127.0.0.1:34080 for 15 s; goodput is measured at the sink. The script below does steps 1–3 (`python3 run.py <sing-box binary> 15`).
4. Repeat with v1.14.4, testing, and testing with the patch above.

<details><summary>run.py</summary>

```python
"""Loopback reproduction for the upstream report: hysteria2 + salamander, upload through the client.

Starts a TCP sink, a sing-box hysteria2 server and client on 127.0.0.1, then pushes data through the
client's mixed inbound (HTTP CONNECT) for a fixed time and reports goodput at the sink.
Usage: python3 run.py <sing-box binary> [seconds]
"""
import json
import os
import shutil
from pathlib import Path
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time

SINK, SERVER, CLIENT = 34500, 34443, 34080


def sink(counter, stop):
    srv = socket.socket(); srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    srv.bind(('127.0.0.1', SINK)); srv.listen(16); srv.settimeout(0.5)
    def drain(conn):
        conn.settimeout(1)
        while not stop.is_set():
            try:
                data = conn.recv(1 << 20)
            except socket.timeout:
                continue
            if not data:
                break
            counter[0] += len(data)
    while not stop.is_set():
        try:
            conn, _ = srv.accept()
        except socket.timeout:
            continue
        threading.Thread(target=drain, args=(conn,), daemon=True).start()
    srv.close()


def push(seconds, flows=4):
    block = os.urandom(1 << 16)
    def one():
        s = socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', CLIENT))
        s.sendall(f'CONNECT 127.0.0.1:{SINK} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:{SINK}\r\n\r\n'.encode())
        reply = s.recv(4096)
        assert b' 200' in reply.split(b'\r\n')[0], reply
        end = time.monotonic() + seconds
        while time.monotonic() < end:
            s.sendall(block)
        s.close()
    threads = [threading.Thread(target=one) for _ in range(flows)]
    for t in threads: t.start()
    for t in threads: t.join()


def main():
    binary, seconds = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 15
    work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='hy2-loop-'))
    # RSA: macOS LibreSSL writes explicit-parameter EC keys that Go's crypto/x509 rejects.
    subprocess.run(['openssl', 'req', '-x509', '-newkey', 'rsa:2048', '-nodes',
                    '-keyout', str(work/'key.pem'), '-out', str(work/'cert.pem'), '-days', '1', '-subj', '/CN=loop.test',
                    '-addext', 'subjectAltName=DNS:loop.test'], check=True, capture_output=True)
    obfs = {'type': 'salamander', 'password': 'loopback-obfs'}
    server = {'log': {'level': 'error'},
              'inbounds': [{'type': 'hysteria2', 'listen': '127.0.0.1', 'listen_port': SERVER, 'obfs': obfs,
                            'users': [{'password': 'loopback'}],
                            'tls': {'enabled': True, 'certificate_path': str(work/'cert.pem'), 'key_path': str(work/'key.pem')}}]}
    client = {'log': {'level': 'error'},
              'inbounds': [{'type': 'mixed', 'listen': '127.0.0.1', 'listen_port': CLIENT}],
              'outbounds': [{'type': 'hysteria2', 'tag': 'hy2', 'server': '127.0.0.1', 'server_port': SERVER,
                             'password': 'loopback', 'obfs': obfs,
                             'tls': {'enabled': True, 'server_name': 'loop.test', 'certificate_path': str(work/'cert.pem')}}],
              'route': {'final': 'hy2'}}
    (work/'server.json').write_text(json.dumps(server)); (work/'client.json').write_text(json.dumps(client))
    procs = [subprocess.Popen([binary, 'run', '-c', str(work/name)]) for name in ('server.json', 'client.json')]
    counter, stop = [0], threading.Event()
    threading.Thread(target=sink, args=(counter, stop), daemon=True).start()
    try:
        time.sleep(1.5)
        push(2)                       # warm-up
        before, t0 = counter[0], time.monotonic()
        push(seconds)
        time.sleep(0.5)
        mbps = (counter[0]-before)*8/(time.monotonic()-t0)/1e6
        print(json.dumps({'binary': os.path.basename(binary), 'upload_mbps': round(mbps, 1), 'seconds': seconds}))
    finally:
        stop.set()
        for p in procs:
            p.terminate(); p.wait(timeout=5)
        shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

The CCM and OCM services read their local credential JSON with filemanager.ReadFile (which falls back to os.ReadFile, or io.ReadAll when a file manager is set) and apply no size limit. A ~2 MiB credential file is fully

/issues?state=open&per_page=8.title: Darwin process lookup can return the previous owner of a reused TCP tuple
/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
### Operating system
macOS

### System version
26.6.2 (25G83), Apple silicon

### Installation type
Library (sing-box embedded as a Go module in a Network Extension)

### Version
v1.14.4; the code is unchanged on `testing` (039d829d, file last touched by f8134779)

### Description
The darwin process lookup can attribute a new TCP connection to the previous owner of the same tuple. The finder caches the PCB snapshot for 200 ms per protocol and accepts an exact cached match as soon as that entry's PID still resolves to a path (https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box/blob/039d829d20c7bfb963dd73113afa9f2d1f080a70/common/process/searcher_darwin_shared.go#L86-L123). If another live process opens a connection with the same tuple inside that window, the stale entry wins. The router additionally caches ownership by tuple for 200 ms (https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box/blob/039d829d20c7bfb963dd73113afa9f2d1f080a70/route/process_cache.go#L13-L35), so both layers would need to treat a new connection as a new lookup.

This is rare with ephemeral ports, but when it happens the result is a wrong owner (another app's `process_path` rule applies), not "not found".

### Reproduction
Measured in a macOS VM through a packet tunnel that calls `FindDarwinConnectionOwner` on each SYN: two processes explicitly bind the same source port and connect to the same destination; the first stays alive. Second SYN 24–164 ms after the first: 9/9 returned the first executable. 258–1012 ms apart: 9/9 returned the correct one.

A deterministic regression test can model two successive PCB snapshots with the same tuple and different live owners: after the first lookup populates the cache, a lookup for the new connection should return its current owner.

I could not reproduce it over loopback alone, because a refused loopback connect leaves the PCB list before the second lookup; it needs a connection still in SYN_SENT.

### Logs
```
pair  gap_ms  expected     got
1     24.1    flowgen-b    flowgen-a
…     …       …            …
9     163.5   flowgen-b    flowgen-a
10    258.1   flowgen-b    flowgen-b
…
18    1012.3  flowgen-b    flowgen-b
```

/issues?state=open&per_page=8.title: Darwin process lookup misses native IPv6 UDP from a dual-stack wildcard socket
/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
### Operating system
macOS

### System version
26.6.2 (25G83), Apple silicon

### Installation type
Library (sing-box embedded as a Go module in a Network Extension; also reproduced with a plain Go program below)

### Version
v1.14.4; the code is unchanged on `testing` (039d829d, file last touched by f8134779)

### Description
`process.FindDarwinConnectionOwner` returns `process not found` for UDP sent over native IPv6 from an unconnected dual-stack socket (`AF_INET6`, `IPV6_V6ONLY=0`, bound to `[::]`). The same socket with `IPV6_V6ONLY=1` is found.

XNU marks a dual-stack wildcard PCB with `INP_IPV4 | INP_IPV6` (https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/f6217f891ac0bb64f3d375211650a4c1ff8ca1ea/bsd/netinet6/udp6_usrreq.c#L867-L884). The snapshot parser checks the IPv4 bit first and keeps only a 32-bit `0.0.0.0`, so the matcher rejects the entry on address width before wildcard matching: https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box/blob/039d829d20c7bfb963dd73113afa9f2d1f080a70/common/process/searcher_darwin_shared.go#L205-L247

Before the snapshot refactor (d2a93378) the family was chosen at lookup time (https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box/blob/3f05a37f65318a155e5795bf6f6f758519409f8d/common/process/searcher_darwin.go#L99-L122, see #3105). Simply checking IPv6 first would break IPv4 lookups against the same wildcard socket; keeping both families for dual-stack wildcard entries would fix both. In practice `process_path` rules silently miss for any app that sends IPv6 UDP from a default `AF_INET6` socket.

### Reproduction
Loopback only, no TUN, no config:

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/sagernet/sing-box/common/process"
)

func main() {
	for _, v6only := range []int{0, 1} {
		fd, _ := syscall.Socket(syscall.AF_INET6, syscall.SOCK_DGRAM, 0)
		syscall.SetsockoptInt(fd, syscall.IPPROTO_IPV6, syscall.IPV6_V6ONLY, v6only)
		syscall.Bind(fd, &syscall.SockaddrInet6{})
		syscall.Sendto(fd, []byte("x"), 0, &syscall.SockaddrInet6{Port: 9, Addr: [16]byte{15: 1}})
		sa, _ := syscall.Getsockname(fd)
		src := netip.AddrPortFrom(netip.MustParseAddr("::1"), uint16(sa.(*syscall.SockaddrInet6).Port))
		owner, err := process.FindDarwinConnectionOwner("udp", src, netip.MustParseAddrPort("[::1]:9"))
		fmt.Println("v6only", v6only, owner, err)
	}
}
```

Output:

```
v6only 0 <nil> process not found
v6only 1 &{... ProcessPath:/path/to/repro ...} <nil>
```

### Logs
```
B udp v6only=0 [::1]:51941 -> [::1]:9: error: process not found
B udp v6only=1 [::1]:61329 -> [::1]:9: path=/…/repro
```

/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.title: Add optional bandwidth-aware mode for urltest
/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.body:
Closes #4397.

## Problem

`urltest` ranks outbounds by a single scalar: time to response headers from a `HEAD`. That is a good proxy for reachability and round-trip latency, but carries no information about sustained throughput. On a congested or shaped path the two decouple — the probe completes before the connection leaves slow start, so it never observes that throughput has collapsed, and the slower outbound is ranked first. No value of `tolerance` can express "prefer the outbound that actually moves data", because every stored sample is latency.

## Approach

An opt-in `bandwidth_test` block, disabled by default. When disabled the probe path is byte-for-byte what it is today: a `HEAD` with no body transfer.

When enabled, each outbound is additionally probed with a bounded `GET`:

- TTFB is recorded with the existing timer semantics, so `delay` keeps its current meaning
- the body is read into one reusable 32 KiB buffer until `max_bytes`, then the request context is cancelled so the remainder is torn down rather than drained
- throughput is `bytes / transfer_time`, excluding TTFB
- both metrics land on `URLTestHistory` and surface through the Clash API

Selection gains two strategies alongside the unchanged default: `throughput`, and `throughput_with_latency_floor` (discard outbounds above the floor, then rank survivors by throughput).

## Design notes

**Bounded, not a benchmark.** A cap in the low hundreds of KiB measures while the flow is still near slow start, so the absolute number understates a fast path. That is acceptable for *ranking* — the ratio between a shaped and unshaped path is already large at that scale — and the docs say so explicitly rather than presenting it as a speed test.

**Memory is independent of the cap.** `max_bytes` bounds bytes *read*, not bytes *retained*; the discard loop uses a single pooled buffer. This is the binding constraint on iOS, where the network extension runs under a hard jetsam limit (#3976).

**Cost control.** Bandwidth probing runs on its own cadence (5× the latency interval by default), with concurrency 2 rather than the latency sweep's fixed 10, and inherits the group's existing idle suspension and `pause.Manager` handling — no probing while the group is unused or the device is asleep.

**Non-2xx is rejected.** A rate-limited endpoint returns a small error page fast, which would otherwise score as excellent throughput (cf. #4189). Note this makes the two probes asymmetric: the latency probe accepts any status, this one requires `2xx`.

**Failure decays rather than evicting.** A failed bandwidth probe records a zero sample and never touches the latency history, so it cannot deselect an outbound the latency probe still considers reachable. Median smoothing over the last N samples absorbs a single transient failure while letting sustained failure decay an outbound out of contention — this is what keeps the group from oscillating and repeatedly firing `interruptGroup.Interrupt`.

**Storage merges instead of replacing.** `StoreURLTestDelay` / `StoreURLTestBandwidth` update one metric while preserving the other, copy-on-write under the lock since readers hold the pointer from `LoadURLTestHistory`. The four existing latency call sites (Clash API ×2, daemon ×2) were switched over so a manually triggered delay test no longer discards throughput.

## Deviation from the issue

The issue argued for **no default `url`**, failing closed. This PR ships one: `https://speed.cloudflare.com/__down?bytes=<max_bytes>`, mirroring how the latency probe defaults to `generate_204`. The byte count is derived from `max_bytes` so the response is exactly as large as the probe reads, and the docs recommend substituting your own endpoint. Happy to revert to fail-closed if you prefer the original reasoning.

Config uses plain numbers (`max_bytes: 262144`, `throughput_tolerance: 25`) rather than the issue's `"256KiB"` / `"25%"` strings, to avoid introducing two new marshalable option types.

## Testing

- `protocol/group`: option validation, median smoothing, relative hysteresis, sliding sample window
- `common/urltest`: the byte cap, non-2xx rejection, empty body, throughput arithmetic, and the storage merge semantics
- `test/urltest_test.go`: end-to-end through real shadowsocks proxies. **`urltest` had no integration coverage at all**, so this adds the baseline too — latency ranking, dropping a failed outbound, `tolerance` holding the incumbent, and `URLTest` reporting delays — before the bandwidth cases.

The headline test encodes the issue's own table: two paths where one answers fast then crawls and the other is slow to first byte but moves data. Same config, only `strategy` differs — `latency` picks the first, `throughput` picks the second. It cannot pass for the wrong reason: with no throughput sample, selection falls back to latency and picks the first.

Ran the integration suite 10× consecutively with no failures. `goleak` (already wired into that package) covers the second ticker's cleanup.

## Two things found along the way

**`minDelay == 0` is a sentinel collision.** In latency `Select`, `minDelay == 0` means "no incumbent yet", but a probe over a fast path genuinely measures 0 ms — so a healthy outbound reads as unset and a *slower* one overrides it. Reproducible over loopback; the integration tests keep every backend above a millisecond to work around it. Pre-existing and independent of this change — happy to file separately or fix here, whichever you prefer.

**An untouched group probes exactly once.** The retry ticker is only created by `Touch()`, so a group that is never dialed probes at `PostStart` and never again; a single transient failure leaves it permanently unselected. Harmless in production since traffic touches the group, but worth knowing.

## Open question

TCP and UDP are selected separately, but there is one probe, dialed over TCP, so UDP selection is ranked by a TCP-measured sample. Defensible for a QUIC outbound sharing the path, less so otherwise. Latency has the same property today, so this is not a regression — but I am happy to restrict throughput ranking to TCP if you would rather be conservative.

## Commits

1. `Repair test module dependency graph` — the `test/` module could not build at all: `gvisor` was pinned to a 2025 revision while `sing-tun` and `tailscale` had moved to versions requiring the current one. Unrelated to the feature, kept separate; verified by moving the new test file aside and reproducing on a clean tree.
2. `Add optional bandwidth-aware mode for urltest` — the feature, tests, and docs (en + zh, plus regenerated `docs/schema.json`).

/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.title: New Endpoint Support: Geph5
/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.body:
This pull request adds a [Geph5](https://github.com/geph-official/geph5) endpoint to sing-box.

Geph5 exposes its VPN transport through a stdio packet protocol. The new endpoint manages the official `geph5-client` process and connects its stdin/stdout packet stream to sing-box's userspace IP stack.

The endpoint supports TCP and UDP through the normal sing-box endpoint interface. DNS resolution intentionally remains in the sing-box routing layer: Geph receives resolved IP destinations, while domains can be resolved by a route rule before dialing the endpoint.

## Configuration

```json
{
  "type": "geph",
  "tag": "geph5",
  "executable_path": "/usr/bin/geph5-client",
  "config_path": "/etc/geph5/client.yaml",
  "control_address": "127.0.0.1:9913",
  "startup_timeout": "15s",
  "extra_args": []
}
```

The `config_path` and `control_address` fields are required. The control address must be a loopback address, must match `control_listen` in the Geph5 configuration, and must be available when the endpoint starts. Because Geph5's TCP control RPC is unauthenticated, it should remain accessible only from the local host.

sing-box supplies `--config` and `--stdio-vpn` when starting the client and rejects attempts to override those managed arguments through `extra_args`.

`startup_timeout` bounds both process launch and readiness polling. sing-box queries the control RPC `conn_info` method and exposes the endpoint only after Geph reports `Connected`.

## Implementation

- Registers the `geph` endpoint and proxy display name.
- Starts `geph5-client` with context cancellation and lifecycle handling.
- Verifies that the configured control address is available before launch.
- Polls the `conn_info` JSON-RPC method until Geph reports `Connected`.
- Validates the RPC version, request ID, result, error, and connection state.
- Reports bounded stderr diagnostics and reaps the child after startup failure, timeout, or cancellation.
- Frames packets with Geph5's 16-bit big-endian length prefix and copies packet buffers across the process boundary.
- Requires endpoint destinations to be resolved IP addresses.
- Exposes TCP and UDP through the existing userspace packet-stack adapter.
- Adds JSON schema entries and English/Chinese endpoint documentation.

The endpoint requires a build with `-tags with_gvisor`, because the userspace IP stack translates sing-box TCP/UDP operations into Geph5's packet stream.

The official Geph exit service applies destination-port restrictions. Those restrictions are lifted for Plus subscribers, so testing an additional outbound proxy chained through the Geph endpoint may require a Plus account.

## Testing

```bash
go test ./protocol/geph
go test -tags with_gvisor ./protocol/geph
go test -race ./protocol/geph
go vet ./protocol/geph
```

The focused Geph tests, race run, vet run, schema validation, and tagged build checks pass.

A repository-wide `go test ./...` run also reaches and passes the Geph package. Its remaining failures are unrelated host/toolchain issues: network-namespace creation is not permitted in `common/netns`, the test host's `/etc/hosts` does not define `localhost` for `dns/transport/hosts`, and `experimental/boxdd` and `experimental/libbox` encounter an existing `runtime/pprof.parseProcSelfMaps` link error.

## Follow-up scope

To keep this review focused, a follow-up pull request will add opt-in `sing-box check --start-geph` validation and graceful shutdown through the Geph control RPC. Those changes are intentionally not included in this pull request.

Thank you very much for taking the time to review this contribution. Feedback is welcome.

/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.title: wireguard: refresh FQDN peer endpoints on handshake retry
/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.body:
WireGuard peer endpoint domains are currently resolved only during startup. When a DDNS record changes, the device keeps sending handshakes to the stale address until sing-box is restarted.

This change listens for wireguard-go handshake retry events and then:

- performs a fresh DNS lookup with the configured resolver and cache disabled;
- updates changed peer endpoints in place through minimal UAPI `update_only` commands;
- coalesces concurrent events and limits refreshes to one every 10 seconds;
- keeps literal-IP peers and healthy/idle tunnels unchanged.

FQDN peers no longer use the fixed-remote connected bind optimization, so an updated address takes effect without recreating the WireGuard device or TUN.

This supersedes the approach in #3486: refreshes are driven by actual WireGuard handshake failure rather than generic connection errors, and cached DNS answers are explicitly bypassed.

Tests:

- `go test -race ./transport/wireguard ./protocol/wireguard`
- `go test -tags "$(cat release/DEFAULT_BUILD_TAGS_OTHERS)" -ldflags "$(cat release/LDFLAGS)" ./...`
- Windows amd64 build with `release/DEFAULT_BUILD_TAGS_WINDOWS`
- Windows `sing-box check` against the production configuration

/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.title: Fix STUN test when server address is an IP literal
/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.body:
## Problem

`stun.Run` assigns two different types to `serverAddr` depending on which branch
it takes (`common/stun/stun.go`):

```go
if options.Dialer != nil {
    packetConn, err = options.Dialer.ListenPacket(ctx, serverSocksaddr)
    serverAddr = serverSocksaddr            // M.Socksaddr
} else {
    serverUDPAddr, _ := net.ResolveUDPAddr("udp", serverSocksaddr.String())
    packetConn, err = net.ListenPacket("udp", "")
    serverAddr = serverUDPAddr              // *net.UDPAddr
}
```

`serverAddr` is then passed to `conn.WriteTo(request, addr)` in `roundTrip`.

When the server is given as a **domain**, `ListenPacketWithDestination` resolves it
and returns a conn wrapped by `N.ListenSerial`, which accepts `M.Socksaddr`. When the
server is given as an **IP literal**, the raw packet conn is returned and the type
mismatch surfaces:

- `net.UDPConn.WriteTo` rejects the address: `write udp4 ...: invalid argument`.
  The STUN test simply does not work.
- `gonet.UDPConn.WriteTo` (gVisor, used by WireGuard and Tailscale endpoints)
  type-asserts to `*net.UDPAddr` and panics, taking down the whole instance:

```
panic: interface conversion: net.Addr is metadata.Socksaddr, not *net.UDPAddr

gvisor/pkg/tcpip/adapters/gonet.(*UDPConn).WriteTo(...)  gonet.go:665
sing-box/common/stun.roundTrip(...)                      common/stun/stun.go:342
sing-box/common/stun.Run(...)                            common/stun/stun.go:452
```

The default server (`stun.voipgate.com:3478`) is a hostname, which is why the
domain-only path has been exercised and the defect stayed hidden.

Originally observed on the iOS graphical client (1.14.0-beta.2) via
Tools -> STUN Test with a WireGuard endpoint selected and an IP address typed into
the Server field; the extension crashed with SIGABRT.

## Fix

Convert to `*net.UDPAddr` when the server is already an IP. The domain case is left
untouched, since that path goes through the wrapper and works today.

Alternatives considered: wrapping the raw packet conn returned by
`Endpoint.ListenPacketWithDestination` for the IP branch, so that it accepts
`M.Socksaddr` the way the domain branch already does via `N.ListenSerial`; or making
`gonet.UDPConn.WriteTo` return an error instead of panicking. Both are broader
changes affecting other callers, so this keeps the fix at the site that produces the
wrong type.

## Reproduction

`createDialer` in `cmd/sing-box/cmd_tools.go` falls back to
`instance.Outbound().Default()` when `-o` is omitted, so `options.Dialer` is never
`nil` on the command line. The shortest reproduction therefore needs no special
configuration at all — any config, any outbound:

```
sing-box tools stun -s 185.125.180.70:3478
# binding request: send STUN request: write udp4 ...: invalid argument
```

For the panic, an endpoint is required (no TUN, no remote server, no graphical
client; the peer never has to answer, because the failure happens on the first
write):

```json
{
  "endpoints": [
    {
      "type": "wireguard",
      "tag": "wg-ep",
      "system": false,
      "address": ["10.0.0.2/32"],
      "private_key": "<generated>",
      "peers": [
        {
          "address": "127.0.0.1",
          "port": 51820,
          "public_key": "<generated>",
          "allowed_ips": ["0.0.0.0/0"]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "outbounds": [{ "type": "direct", "tag": "direct" }]
}
```

```
sing-box tools stun -o wg-ep -s 185.125.180.70:3478   # panic
```

Note: reaching the endpoint case from the command line requires one local change —
`createPreStartedClient` in `cmd/sing-box/cmd_tools.go` calls `instance.PreStart()`,
while `Endpoint.started` is only set at `StartStatePostStart`, so every `tools`
command against a WireGuard or Tailscale endpoint currently fails with
`WireGuard is not ready yet`. Replacing `PreStart()` with `Start()` locally makes the
panic reproducible on the CLI. That is a separate concern and is not part of this
change.

## Verification

Built from v1.14.0-beta.2 with `-tags with_gvisor,with_wireguard`, go1.26.

| outbound | server     | before             | after                                                |
| -------- | ---------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `direct` | IP literal | `invalid argument` | external address, latency, NAT mapping and filtering |
| `direct` | hostname   | works              | works                                                |
| `wg-ep`  | IP literal | panic              | fails cleanly (`i/o timeout`, peer is a stub)        |
| `wg-ep`  | hostname   | `i/o timeout`      | `i/o timeout`                                        |

/issues?state=open&per_page=8.title: Extended cold-boot / shutdown timing services causes `DKOMBI4` to lose cached vehicle model and revert to X5 G05 fallback
/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
### Problem Description

On a **BMW G30 LCI** (`HU_MGU` on `030_016_002`), after rooting the head unit and installing `mgu-store`, waking the car up from deep sleep (*Parken*, >15 minutes) causes the instrument cluster (`DKOMBI4`) to display the generic silver/white **X5 G05 fallback asset** for several seconds before switching to the actual G30 LCI visualization once the MGU finishes booting.

Normally, `DKOMBI4` caches the last received vehicle model and color in NVRAM (`3004 ERM_Konfiguration`, with `KOMBI_SYNC_FAIL_CAR_MODEL*` set to `aktiv`) so it can render the correct car from frame 1 while waiting for `HU_MGU` to complete its cold boot.

Further testing revealed a specific pattern around shutdown and wake timing:

* **Workaround that temporarily restored the cache:** Waking the car, letting infotainment fully initialize, exiting and closing the doors **without locking for 4–5 minutes** (allowing `DKOMBI4` to complete its *Nachlauf* flash write before Terminal 30B drops), and then locking for another 15 minutes (_Parken_ state). On the next cold wake-up, the G30 LCI appeared immediately from frame 1.


* **Trigger that broke it again:** Going for a normal drive (ignition on - `KL15` state) and **locking the car immediately** upon exiting consistently wiped/invalidated the cluster's cached model, bringing the X5 G05 fallback back on the next deep-sleep wake-up.



---

### Troubleshooting & A/B Isolation Steps

To isolate whether this was caused by the SSH root (`idrive7-8-ssh-root`), `SWFL_000056EA` (`winston`), or `mgu-store`, I performed the following steps in sequence:

1. **Disabled SSH root via the GUI app** (`31 02 A0 FD` + removing `/etc` persistence) — **Did not help**.


2. **Uninstalled all Store apps via the in-car ID7 Store UI** (leaving core `mgu-store`, `mgu-updater`, `mgu-deploy`, and tools without an uninstall button intact) — **Did not help**.


3. **Flashed only `SWFL_000056EA_030_016_002` (stock `winston` binary) via E-Sys** — **Did not help**.


4. **Ran the PC `mgu-store` uninstall script + flashed all 14 `SWFL` binaries via E-Sys** — **Fixed the issue completely**; cluster graphics returned to normal.


5. **Re-rooted the MGU using the latest `idrive7-8-ssh-root` GUI (`Flash + Enable`) without `mgu-store` installed** — **Graphics remain intact** even after normal drives, immediate locking, deep sleep cycles, and `KL15` ignition cycles.



This confirms that **clean SSH root alone does not cause the issue**. Something in the `mgu-store` native background services/boot hooks delays startup or interferes with the clean shutdown handshake between `HU_MGU` (`winston` / `SOME/IP`) and `DKOMBI4`.

---

### Findings from Code Inspection (manually instructed Gemini Hydrogen)

Reviewing the `mgu-store` systemd units, shell scripts, and daemon code points to three specific bottlenecks during cold boot and shutdown (while ruling out firewall interference):

1. **Heavy synchronous Node.js execution on every boot (`mgu-app-fallback.service`):**
* `mgu-app-fallback.service` runs as `Type=oneshot` with `Before=oapcontroller.service app-privacy.service`.
* On **every single cold boot**, its `ExecStart` sequentially spawns **four separate `/usr/bin/node` (Node 8) processes** to parse, patch, syntax-check (`node --check`), and byte-compare (`node -e`) the multi-megabyte `main.bundle.js` before bind-mounting it.
* On the MGU's embedded ARM CPU and flash storage, running four V8 instances sequentially during early userspace init saturates CPU and I/O right when `HmiMain3D` / `winston` (`SWFL_000056EA`) and `SOME/IP` need to initialize and sync with `DKOMBI4`.


* Additionally, `ExecStop` runs `umount` on `main.bundle.js`, which can contend with `oapcontroller.service` teardown during rapid Terminal 30B shutdowns when locking immediately after driving.


2. **Full widget directory copy on every boot (`mgu-render-hmi.sh`):**
* In `boot` mode (before `hmi.service` starts), `mgu-render-hmi.sh` hashes `.pbw` files and performs a full recursive copy (`cp -a`) of `/mnt/dataro/data/hmi/bmw/widget` into `/run/mgu-render/hmi-widget` on every cold start before bind-mounting it, directly delaying `HmiMain3D` / `winston` startup.


3. **Early startup of background daemons (`mgu-updater.service` & `mgu-uplink.service`):**
* Both units specify `After=local-fs.target` and `WantedBy=multi-user.target`.
* Even with `Nice=10` on `mgu-updater`, both services initialize and perform I/O on `/var/opt` concurrently with critical automotive networking (`IPsec` / `charon` / `SOME/IP`) and HMI rendering, despite not being needed during the first 15–20 seconds of vehicle wake-up.




4. **Ruled out: `nftables` firewall rules (`firewall.go`):**
* Inspection of `firewall.go` confirms that `mgu-uplink` creates an isolated `inet mgu_uplink` table with `policy accept` defaults and scopes all `drop` / `accept` rules strictly to `iifname` / `oifname` of the external USB/Wi-Fi uplink interface. Internal Automotive Ethernet / VLAN and `xfrm` (`IPsec`) traffic between `HU_MGU` and `DKOMBI4` is completely untouched.





---

### Proposed Solutions (by Gemini Hydrogen)

To eliminate boot/shutdown contention with `HU_MGU` ↔ `DKOMBI4` synchronization:

1. **Skip redundant Node.js runs in `mgu-app-fallback.service`:**
* Store a lightweight hash or `stat` signature (timestamp + size) of the stock `main.bundle.js` and `custom_apps.json` in `/bin/sh`.
* Only invoke `fallback_build.js`, `patch_mainapp.js`, and `node --check` when the underlying bundle or app list has actually changed (e.g., after an app install/update or I-Step update), and go straight to `mount --bind` on routine cold boots.


2. **Defer `mgu-updater.service` and `mgu-uplink.service` startup:**
* Change `After=local-fs.target` to `After=hmi.service` (or add a short `ExecStartPre=/bin/sleep 15`) so neither daemon competes for CPU or `/var/opt` flash I/O during the critical `SOME/IP` / `winston` handshake window with `DKOMBI4`.




3. **Optimize widget mounting in `mgu-render-hmi.sh`:**
* Consider using `overlayfs` (if supported by the MGU kernel) or symlinking unmodified stock widgets instead of copying the entire `/mnt/dataro/data/hmi/bmw/widget` directory into `/run` on every boot.

**AI**: Asisted by Gemini Hydrogen (issue wording, instructed code review, drafted solution).

/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.title: mgu-updater: verify backup source downloads against GitHub catalogs
/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.body:
GitHub package downloads can be unreliable even when a nearby HTTPS copy is reachable. This adds an optional **Backup source** on the phone page for GitHub release catalogs, including the Store's built-in source. The original GitHub source retains its identity, listing, versions, dependencies, build instructions and icons. No regional service is bundled or enabled by default.

Refs #197, especially the version/content parity requirement in https://github.com/robertnisipeanu/mgu-store/issues/197#issuecomment-6943132029.

The backup catalog supplies download locations only. Its selected entry must match GitHub's id, kind, version, package name, size and SHA-256; downloaded bytes are checked against GitHub's size and digest before reaching the deploy tool. A mirror-provided hash cannot establish trust. Modified/localized packages must remain separate sources. Missing, mismatched or unavailable backup packages either fail or fall back to the exact verified GitHub package, according to the owner's checkbox. HTTPS-only fetching, redirect checks and token isolation remain in force.

Each Check attempts an official catalog refresh. A separate root-only snapshot, bound to the GitHub repository and releases channel, permits outage reuse for at most **24 hours** without extending its timestamp. Missing, expired, future-dated or invalid verification requires reaching GitHub; installation fails if verification cannot be obtained. The phone page shows the verification time. Queued packages whose version/digest/size/dependencies no longer match are rejected. Dependencies retain their own source settings and existing installation order.

**Review decision:** This draft proposes a 24-hour maximum age for outage reuse. It guarantees parity with a bounded-age official snapshot, not that an unreachable upstream has no newer release. Please review that freshness policy before accepting this design. Initial use still needs access to GitHub; this does not bootstrap trust from an untrusted mirror.

Only mgu-updater needs updating; the existing Store opens its phone page. Versions, default sources and deployment protocols are unchanged. Branch/tag and digest-less release listings cannot use backup transport. Configuration preserves source ids, origins, builtin status and channel; edits wait for an idle queue/check. PR #281's channel-editing work was reviewed for overlap: this uses a separate operation, and a backup must be turned off before selecting a branch/tag channel. The branch is based directly on official main 6e80c4d and contains no CN version, domain, localization or release-channel changes.

**AI:** Codex, GPT-6 — implementation, tests, documentation and PR preparation.

**Tested:** In a dedicated Lima Linux VM (`mgu-backup-test`), Docker `node:8.16.2-stretch`, running as root: `native/mgu-updater/test/run.sh` completed, including certificates, UIDs, proxy (41 passed), updater (642 passed / 0 failed), web (23 passed), page and backup tests. The updater suite includes a real local HTTPS/redirect integration exercising authenticated configuration of the built-in source, verified package bytes and disabling the backup. After the final cache/UI guard edits, `test_backup.js` (42 checks) and `test_page.js` were rerun on Node 8.16.2. The focused checks cover tampered bytes, mismatched versions/kinds/digests/sizes, poisoned mirror metadata, absent/expired/future/corrupt/wrong-repo trust caches, restart, fallback policy, dependency changes, URL validation and authorization. `node release/release.js versions origin/main` and `git diff --check` passed. Playwright Chromium exercised saving and disabling the phone configuration with synthetic local API state.

The proxy scenario emits an unhandled-promise warning for an absent deploy command; the same warning was independently reproduced in the unchanged upstream proxy scenario at 6e80c4d (8 assertions passed). No real car was tested or connected. **Head-unit emulator and on-unit upgrade-order testing are not done**: no local `mgu-emulator/emu.py` was available and the named emulator repository could not be read anonymously. /issues?state=open&per_page=8.title: waze-on-cluster: patch any car with a cluster display; Not supported only where the patch can't apply
/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
## What

**CarPlay and Android Auto patches on any car with a cluster display.** An install applies both patches wherever the locator finds and verifies their sites, whatever KI_KOMBI_VARIANT the car is coded with. A car whose coding can't be read is patched too. A first patch is on trial and under boot recovery, as on any car.
- **CarPlay:** the plan remaps the car's own coding slot in the converter's jump table to IC_HIGH (`variant-<n>`, for 1–6, 8, 10 and 11), as well as slot 7. 9 is IC_HIGH as shipped. An unreadable coding is planned as 7.
- **Android Auto:** the cluster geometry goes in aapd.conf under the screen size aapd looks the coding up by: 10.25 for coding 10, otherwise 12.3.
- **Coding 0 (no cluster display):** refused. It is the only coding that is.
- **At the boot step:** a plan still to be made waits for a readable coding. The watcher makes it after its own wait, whatever the coding then reads.

**No patch carries across a car software update.**
- A plan still to be made is dropped when the service's build-id has changed. After an update replaces carplay or aapd, they run as they ship until the next install or Patch.
- Remove patch stays off across the update.

**Android Auto on aapd builds without the ready-start edit.**
- The `readystart` edit (added in 0.14.0) is planned only where it is found and verifies. Elsewhere the plan has the other edits, and the overlay reports `readystart: NOT APPLIED (<reason>)`.
- Every aapd build that 0.13.x could patch in memory can be patched in memory again, with the same verification of the other sites.

**Status texts.** The Status rows say Not supported only where the patch can't be applied, and give the reason. A patch turned off with Remove patch reads `Removed`; this includes a patch turned off with an earlier release's Remove patch, before it ran in memory. Every new text is translated in all 32 locales.

| State | Status shown |
|---|---|
| Head unit the tool refuses, or no Android Auto on it | `Not supported on this head unit` (was `Not supported on this car`) |
| Car coded with no cluster display (KI_KOMBI_VARIANT 0) | `Not supported — no cluster display` (was `Not supported on this car`) |
| Build whose sites the patcher can't find or verify | `Not supported — this CarPlay version` / `Not supported — this Android Auto version` (was `Not supported on this car`) |
| Car coded other than 7 (1–6, 8–11) or unreadable coding | `Patched after restart`, then `Patched` (was `Not supported on this car`) |
| Patch turned off with Remove patch | `Removed` (was `Not patched`) |
| In-memory plan that can't be used | `Failed, in-memory plan unusable: <reason>` (was `Changed by another tool`) |

## Why

On cars coded other than KI_KOMBI_VARIANT 7, the patch could be applied but the install wouldn't apply it, and both sections read `Not supported on this car`. On aapd builds without the ready-start site, the Android Auto patch was refused although every edit the map needs was there.

## AI

Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5.

## Tested

**Node suites.**
- `make test-node` passes with real carplay and aapd binaries (`CARPLAY_BIN`, `AAPD_BIN`, `AAPD_CONF`). The suites the last commits touch were run again after them: recovery 112/112, patchd_activate, patch, patchd_patch, inmem and head_unit.
- Two checks fail on this host in the same way on `main`:
  - recovery's "in about a second" timing check (the aapd boot step takes about 2.1 s against a 2 s bound);
  - aapd_test's 10 s density-spacing wait.

**App suites.** `test_control`, `test_page`, `test_profiles` and `test_i18n` pass (32 locales).

**New tests that fail without the change:**
- install and plan on codings 4, 9, 10 and unreadable;
- coding 0 refused;
- `variant-<n>` in the plan and in memory;
- a file with a coded slot already remapped is not pristine;
- aapd 10.25 geometry for coding 10;
- aapd without readystart;
- a plan to make dropped after a build change;
- the boot step leaving a plan to the watcher until the coding reads;
- `Removed` from patchd's status, and from an earlier release's Remove patch;
- each app status text.

**Test unit coded KI_KOMBI_VARIANT 4** (iDrive 7, MGU P18_23w44.2-1-3, aapd 22.39.3):
- With 0.14.18 and app 0.6.17 installed from the Store's artifacts, the install left CarPlay and aapd alone with `not supported on this car (KI_KOMBI_VARIANT 4)`, and both Status rows read `Not supported on this car`.
- This branch was then installed as an update, packaged locally as tool 0.14.19 and app 0.6.18, with no head-unit restart:
  - The install planned and armed both on trial. CarPlay's edits include `variant-4`, and aapd's screen is 12.3.
  - Both rows read `Patched after restart`.
  - Remove patch on each then read `Removed`.
- In an earlier run with the same coding, the next head-unit start ran carplay with `variant` and `variant-4` patched in memory, and the library's result was `applied`.

**Not tested:**
- No phone was connected, so the map itself wasn't seen on a cluster coded other than 7.
- Not run on a real car.
- Not run on an aapd build without the ready-start edit. A test covers that case with the site altered.

## Human review

None before opening.

The app on a test unit coded KI_KOMBI_VARIANT 4.

The default, 250x90 at 110,320, is measured on the G30 LCI; on other cars the driver moves it with the Speed area buttons. The app requires the next waze-on-cluster. **Downgrade:** a profile set with Map size above 100 % does not load in an older patchd (it takes 20-100), so that driver's settings are lost, and an older render falls back to the standard size. /issues?state=open&per_page=8.title: waze-on-cluster, app: a turn card over the cluster map
/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
A turn card: the next manoeuvre (an arrow, the distance and the road) drawn over the cluster map, **below the position arrow** (one line, under the street name the phone writes there) or **at the top** of the map (two lines). It is off unless turned on in the app, and it shows only with the map on the cluster's map slot at its own size (not hosted, not scaled, not on the HUD).

**What it shows.** While the BMW navigation guides, CarPlay's guidance included, the card shows the next manoeuvre as the cluster's own route box has it. waze-on-cluster reads GuidanceEventList (SOME/IP 0xFB1B, event 0x8002) and whether the navigation guides (Guidance 0xFB1A, event 0x8015) as uid 5000, the way the HMI does, and only reads (`src/guidance_link.h`, `src/route_box.h`). It knows turns (straight on, left, slight, sharp, right, U-turn), forks (keep left or right), roundabouts (the exit's angle and number) and the destination (its side), with distances in metres or kilometres. A kind not seen on a drive yet (a ferry, a motorway entry) gets a plain mark with the distance and the road, and the log names its number once, never the road. While the navigation guides, the box empties now and then (a route's start, a recalculation); through those spells the card keeps an instruction with no distance, such as the route's "towards …", and one with a distance for 2.5 s (`src/guided_card.h`).

**Drawing.** `src/turn_card.h`: arrows in BMW's style (the way to go heavy and white, the roads not taken grey) and antialiased Roboto 2.137 rendered ahead of time (`src/card_font.h`, `tools/card_font.py`; Apache License 2.0, `native/waze-on-cluster/LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt`), with Latin, Greek and Cyrillic letters. A line that does not fit ends in an ellipsis. Only the rectangle of the pixels that changed is sent. `make build/host/turn_card_preview` draws every kind of card as one picture.

**App.** The main page gets **Turn card** (Off, Below the arrow, At the top), which waze-on-cluster keeps in `turn_card_state_file`, and **Show an example**, an example card for 10 seconds. The example goes over the navigation's card for 12 s at most, since the app's own end does not come while its page is in the background (`src/card_choice.h`). The new words are in every locale. The app requires the waze-on-cluster released with it (`"next"` in its `release.json`).

`src/keys.cpp` defines every settings key the shipped conf sets, so a new key cannot stop the tool at start: `test/keys_test.cpp` loads the shipped conf the way the program does.

**The phone's own turn card** (the second commit, for vijay38454's report on this pull request). With the turn card on, Apple Maps drew its own manoeuvre card in the CarPlay map below ours: Edit 6's ShowUI asks the phone for its full cluster page, `maps:/car/instrumentcluster?showETA=yes`. While the card shows (Below the arrow or At the top), the patch asks for `maps:/car/instrumentcluster/map` instead, the map alone that Edit 5 already gives the display; Apple Maps' arrival-time card goes with it. There is no new setting: with the Turn card off, everything is as before. The map URL sits at the same place in Edit 6's log text, NULs after it, and the call site is the same (`carplay_locate.js`, PATCH.md "Edit 6"). patchd plans it from the render's saved choice (`turn_card_state_file`): at the Patch button, an install and boot recovery's plan, and on the app's new `{"cmd":"turn-card"}`, which the app sends once the render shows a new choice. That one restarts carplay where patchd may, as the Patch button does, so the phone gets the new URL at once; where it may not, and at an install, carplay keeps running the patch, which patchd counts as patched with nothing pending, and asks for the new URL from its next start. A patch planned again for the other URL stays proven, since only the URL the phone is asked for differs. Being a commit of its own, it can be reviewed, or left out, apart from the card.

A new feature: patch is fine, or `release:minor` if you prefer.

**AI:** Claude Code: Claude Opus 5.5 read the navigation's messages in my car's captures and wrote the change, its tests and this description; Claude Fable 5.2 wrote the first draft of the card's drawing (`src/turn_card.h` and `src/turn_card.cpp`).

/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
Yandex Maps can place its guidance UI incorrectly in the standard CarPlay cluster safe area. Add a Guidance area selector with Default and Yandex Maps (experimental), keeping Default as the initial setting and allowing the owner to return to it.

The Yandex profile uses 504x368+433+72 instead of 504x368+286+72 in the existing 1088x480 frame.

- Feed the selected rectangle into the existing `carplay_patch.js --safe` in-memory plan. `/usr/bin/carplay` stays pristine.
- Persist the choice independently of driver profiles. Reconcile it during installation and boot, including an interrupted profile change; selecting a profile with the patch off does not enable the map.
- Keep other plan arguments and existing custom CLI geometry when no profile has been saved. Compare the actual safe area against the selected profile so the Yandex setting is not reported as an outdated patch.
- Add UI/localization, integration tests and concise documentation. The selection is manual and global to all CarPlay navigation apps; Android Auto is unchanged.

**Release:** Version numbers are intentionally unchanged, as required by CONTRIBUTING.md. Please assign the appropriate versions through the normal release process when this is merged/released. The app requires `waze-on-cluster: "next"` so the release resolves the dependency to the tool published with this change. Local test-build version numbers are not part of this PR.

**AI:** OpenAI Codex, GPT-6 — implementation, automated tests and independent AI code reviews.

/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.title: waze-on-cluster: patch any car with a cluster display; Not supported only where the patch can't apply
/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.body:
## What

**CarPlay and Android Auto patches on any car with a cluster display.** An install applies both patches wherever the locator finds and verifies their sites, whatever KI_KOMBI_VARIANT the car is coded with. A car whose coding can't be read is patched too. A first patch is on trial and under boot recovery, as on any car.
- **CarPlay:** the plan remaps the car's own coding slot in the converter's jump table to IC_HIGH (`variant-<n>`, for 1–6, 8, 10 and 11), as well as slot 7. 9 is IC_HIGH as shipped. An unreadable coding is planned as 7.
- **Android Auto:** the cluster geometry goes in aapd.conf under the screen size aapd looks the coding up by: 10.25 for coding 10, otherwise 12.3.
- **Coding 0 (no cluster display):** refused. It is the only coding that is.
- **At the boot step:** a plan still to be made waits for a readable coding. The watcher makes it after its own wait, whatever the coding then reads.

**No patch carries across a car software update.**
- A plan still to be made is dropped when the service's build-id has changed. After an update replaces carplay or aapd, they run as they ship until the next install or Patch.
- Remove patch stays off across the update.

**Android Auto on aapd builds without the ready-start edit.**
- The `readystart` edit (added in 0.14.0) is planned only where it is found and verifies. Elsewhere the plan has the other edits, and the overlay reports `readystart: NOT APPLIED (<reason>)`.
- Every aapd build that 0.13.x could patch in memory can be patched in memory again, with the same verification of the other sites.

**Status texts.** The Status rows say Not supported only where the patch can't be applied, and give the reason. A patch turned off with Remove patch reads `Removed`; this includes a patch turned off with an earlier release's Remove patch, before it ran in memory. Every new text is translated in all 32 locales.

| State | Status shown |
|---|---|
| Head unit the tool refuses, or no Android Auto on it | `Not supported on this head unit` (was `Not supported on this car`) |
| Car coded with no cluster display (KI_KOMBI_VARIANT 0) | `Not supported — no cluster display` (was `Not supported on this car`) |
| Build whose sites the patcher can't find or verify | `Not supported — this CarPlay version` / `Not supported — this Android Auto version` (was `Not supported on this car`) |
| Car coded other than 7 (1–6, 8–11) or unreadable coding | `Patched after restart`, then `Patched` (was `Not supported on this car`) |
| Patch turned off with Remove patch | `Removed` (was `Not patched`) |
| In-memory plan that can't be used | `Failed, in-memory plan unusable: <reason>` (was `Changed by another tool`) |

## Why

On cars coded other than KI_KOMBI_VARIANT 7, the patch could be applied but the install wouldn't apply it, and both sections read `Not supported on this car`. On aapd builds without the ready-start site, the Android Auto patch was refused although every edit the map needs was there.

## AI

Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5.

## Tested

**Node suites.**
- `make test-node` passes with real carplay and aapd binaries (`CARPLAY_BIN`, `AAPD_BIN`, `AAPD_CONF`). The suites the last commits touch were run again after them: recovery 112/112, patchd_activate, patch, patchd_patch, inmem and head_unit.
- Two checks fail on this host in the same way on `main`:
  - recovery's "in about a second" timing check (the aapd boot step takes about 2.1 s against a 2 s bound);
  - aapd_test's 10 s density-spacing wait.

**App suites.** `test_control`, `test_page`, `test_profiles` and `test_i18n` pass (32 locales).

**New tests that fail without the change:**
- install and plan on codings 4, 9, 10 and unreadable;
- coding 0 refused;
- `variant-<n>` in the plan and in memory;
- a file with a coded slot already remapped is not pristine;
- aapd 10.25 geometry for coding 10;
- aapd without readystart;
- a plan to make dropped after a build change;
- the boot step leaving a plan to the watcher until the coding reads;
- `Removed` from patchd's status, and from an earlier release's Remove patch;
- each app status text.

**Test unit coded KI_KOMBI_VARIANT 4** (iDrive 7, MGU P18_23w44.2-1-3, aapd 22.39.3):
- With 0.14.18 and app 0.6.17 installed from the Store's artifacts, the install left CarPlay and aapd alone with `not supported on this car (KI_KOMBI_VARIANT 4)`, and both Status rows read `Not supported on this car`.
- This branch was then installed as an update, packaged locally as tool 0.14.19 and app 0.6.18, with no head-unit restart:
  - The install planned and armed both on trial. CarPlay's edits include `variant-4`, and aapd's screen is 12.3.
  - Both rows read `Patched after restart`.
  - Remove patch on each then read `Removed`.
- In an earlier run with the same coding, the next head-unit start ran carplay with `variant` and `variant-4` patched in memory, and the library's result was `applied`.

**Not tested:**
- No phone was connected, so the map itself wasn't seen on a cluster coded other than 7.
- Not run on a real car.
- Not run on an aapd build without the ready-start edit. A test covers that case with the site altered.

/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.title: waze-on-cluster, app: a turn card over the cluster map
/pulls?state=open&per_page=5.body:
A turn card: the next manoeuvre (an arrow, the distance and the road) drawn over the cluster map, **below the position arrow** (one line, under the street name the phone writes there) or **at the top** of the map (two lines). It is off unless turned on in the app, and it shows only with the map on the cluster's map slot at its own size (not hosted, not scaled, not on the HUD).

**What it shows.** While the BMW navigation guides, CarPlay's guidance included, the card shows the next manoeuvre as the cluster's own route box has it. waze-on-cluster reads GuidanceEventList (SOME/IP 0xFB1B, event 0x8002) and whether the navigation guides (Guidance 0xFB1A, event 0x8015) as uid 5000, the way the HMI does, and only reads (`src/guidance_link.h`, `src/route_box.h`). It knows turns (straight on, left, slight, sharp, right, U-turn), forks (keep left or right), roundabouts (the exit's angle and number) and the destination (its side), with distances in metres or kilometres. A kind not seen on a drive yet (a ferry, a motorway entry) gets a plain mark with the distance and the road, and the log names its number once, never the road. While the navigation guides, the box empties now and then (a route's start, a recalculation); through those spells the card keeps an instruction with no distance, such as the route's "towards …", and one with a distance for 2.5 s (`src/guided_card.h`).

**Drawing.** `src/turn_card.h`: arrows in BMW's style (the way to go heavy and white, the roads not taken grey) and antialiased Roboto 2.137 rendered ahead of time (`src/card_font.h`, `tools/card_font.py`; Apache License 2.0, `native/waze-on-cluster/LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt`), with Latin, Greek and Cyrillic letters. A line that does not fit ends in an ellipsis. Only the rectangle of the pixels that changed is sent. `make build/host/turn_card_preview` draws every kind of card as one picture.

**App.** The main page gets **Turn card** (Off, Below the arrow, At the top), which waze-on-cluster keeps in `turn_card_state_file`, and **Show an example**, an example card for 10 seconds. The example goes over the navigation's card for 12 s at most, since the app's own end does not come while its page is in the background (`src/card_choice.h`). The new words are in every locale. The app requires the waze-on-cluster released with it (`"next"` in its `release.json`).

`src/keys.cpp` defines every settings key the shipped conf sets, so a new key cannot stop the tool at start: `test/keys_test.cpp` loads the shipped conf the way the program does.

**The phone's own turn card** (the second commit, for vijay38454's report on this pull request). With the turn card on, Apple Maps drew its own manoeuvre card in the CarPlay map below ours: Edit 6's ShowUI asks the phone for its full cluster page, `maps:/car/instrumentcluster?showETA=yes`. While the card shows (Below the arrow or At the top), the patch asks for `maps:/car/instrumentcluster/map` instead, the map alone that Edit 5 already gives the display; Apple Maps' arrival-time card goes with it. There is no new setting: with the Turn card off, everything is as before. The map URL sits at the same place in Edit 6's log text, NULs after it, and the call site is the same (`carplay_locate.js`, PATCH.md "Edit 6"). patchd plans it from the render's saved choice (`turn_card_state_file`): at the Patch button, an install and boot recovery's plan, and on the app's new `{"cmd":"turn-card"}`, which the app sends once the render shows a new choice. That one restarts carplay where patchd may, as the Patch button does, so the phone gets the new URL at once; where it may not, and at an install, carplay keeps running the patch, which patchd counts as patched with nothing pending, and asks for the new URL from its next start. A patch planned again for the other URL stays proven, since only the URL the phone is asked for differs. Being a commit of its own, it can be reviewed, or left out, apart from the card.

A new feature: patch is fine, or `release:minor` if you prefer.

**AI:** Claude Code: Claude Opus 5.5 read the navigation's messages in my car's captures and wrote the change, its tests and this description; Claude Fable 5.2 wrote the first draft of the card's drawing (`src/turn_card.h` and `src/turn_card.cpp`).

/issues?state=open&per_page=8.title: [FEATURE REQUEST] Faster app opening: optional start with the car, with a RAM note
/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
### The problem

Opening an app from the drawer or a shortcut button shows "Loading app" for 5 to 10 seconds on my G20, and sometimes the tap does nothing at all. Switching between two apps I use together (Live Data and Fault Scanner) has the same wait every time.

As far as I can read the code, that is the cold start: apps without `"autostart": true` are started by MainApp only when tapped, so each open starts Node, the SDK and the app from nothing. The four apps that have it (Ambient Config, eDrive, Redline, Warm-Up) are started with the car and open at once.

### The idea

Let the user choose which apps start with the car:

- A setting in every app, for example "Start with the car" (default off). Since `mguAppStartType` is written to package.json at build time (kit/tools/build.py), the Store's deploy tool would probably have to rewrite it when the setting changes. I don't know whether MainApp re-reads it without a reinstall; you know that part better.
- An app started this way stays idle until its page is shown, like Fault Scanner already does (nothing on the car's buses while nobody is on its page).
- A clear note next to the setting: every app kept running uses RAM (up to its `memoryKB`, 192 MB by default), and the head unit stops apps that go over the limit. So start only the two or three apps you really use.

### Alongside it, independent of autostart

- Draw the first screen before the heavy parts load (for Fault Scanner the fault text database, for others fonts or tables), so the wait is shorter even on a cold start.
- Write the start-up times to the app's log (process start, `registered active`, first frame). That way we can measure where the seconds go on a real car before changing anything. I am happy to collect those from my car.

If you agree with the direction, I can send a PR for the kit part (the setting, the note, the idle start and the timings).

Hello developers,

### Vehicle information

- Vehicle: 2021 BMW 3 Series 325 M Sport (China-market Yaoye edition)

2. Enabled SSH access.
3. Installed MGU Store.

5. Subsequently noticed abnormal audio distribution.

- The front dashboard speakers are disproportionately loud.
- The rear speakers produce very low audio output.
- The front-to-rear sound distribution is severely unbalanced.

This is not simply a subjective reduction in sound quality. There is a noticeable difference in output volume between the front and rear speakers.

### Expected behavior

The original front/rear audio balance and factory surround sound behavior should be restored while retaining root access, SSH and MGU Store functionality.

### Possible causes

After reading the related discussions, I suspect that the issue may involve one or more of the following:

- Incomplete HU_MGU coding restoration by BimmerCode.
- An audio system configuration mismatch between HU_MGU and RAM.
- Incorrect AUDIO_SYSTEM coding.
- Missing RAM microphone calibration.
- Incorrect audio channel mapping or amplifier configuration.

3. Which HU_MGU and RAM coding parameters should be checked?
4. Would restoring the original coding using E-Sys resolve this issue?
5. Is ISTA RAM microphone calibration necessary if DTC B7F500 is present?
6. Are there any read-only SSH diagnostic commands or relevant audio logs that could help identify the problem?
7. Is there a recommended recovery procedure that preserves root, SSH and installed applications without reflashing the MGU?

/issues?state=open&per_page=8.title: [FEATURE REQUEST] Exhaust flaps and other details. (sound related)
/issues?state=open&per_page=8.body:
Hi!

First of all, great app, I use it all the time. I have a feature request that I think a lot of owners of OPF/GPF-equipped cars would find useful.

REQUEST
Add OPF (Otto Particulate Filter) data to the Exhaust Flaps screen, or as a separate OPF page next to it. Warmup or M Stats would also work if it fits better there.

WHY
On my car the exhaust sound changes a lot from drive to drive, even in Sport+ with the flap coded always-open. Sometimes it sounds great, sometimes it sounds like a regular car. The most likely cause is the OPF state: when it's loaded with soot it muffles the sound much more, and after a regeneration it opens up. Right now there's no easy way to see this live, so it would be great to see the OPF state right next to the flap status.

DATA THAT WOULD BE USEFUL (all from the DME, which already calculates these values)
1. Calculated soot load (g, and/or % of max)
2. Ash load (g), as a long-term health indicator
3. OPF differential pressure (mbar/hPa)
4. Exhaust gas temperature before the OPF (and after, if available)
5. Regeneration status: active / requested / not active
6. Distance and/or time since last regeneration
7. Regeneration counter (total number of regens, if exposed)
8. Exhaust flap status (already in the app), shown on the same screen for context

UI IDEAS
- Simple gauge or bar for soot load, with color zones (green / yellow / red)
- A clear "REGEN ACTIVE" indicator. It's useful to know so you don't shut the car off mid-regen
- Optional: a small graph of soot load over the drive, so you can see it drop during a regeneration
- Optional: include these values in the existing logging/export so they can be compared with other data

MY CAR (for testing)
- 2019 BMW G20 330i, pre-LCI, EUR-spec
- Engine: B48D (TU1), Euro 6d-TEMP with OPF as standard
- DME: Bosch MG1CS003
- Transmission: ZF 8HP51
- Mods: exhaust flap coded always-open (BimmerCode), FTP charge pipe and intake

The same data should be available on most G-series cars with OPF (B48, B58, S58, etc.), so it's not just for my car.

I'm happy to beta test and send screenshots or logs if that helps. Thanks a lot!

Danijel
